# Taxonic — Full Product and Developer Reference

> Taxonic is an automated semantic classification engine for publishers, libraries, bookstores, distributors, universities, and EdTech platforms. It converts unstructured text and descriptive metadata for books and educational assets into standardized subject classifications.

- Product website: https://usetaxonic.com
- Production API host: https://api.usetaxonic.com
- API reference: https://usetaxonic.com/api
- API Playground / trial: https://usetaxonic.com/api-playground
- Demo: https://usetaxonic.com/demo
- FAQ: https://usetaxonic.com/faq
- Support email: support@contactous.com
- Company named in the website footer: Contactous Pte Ltd.

## 1. Product Overview

Taxonic is an automated cataloging and classification engine. It accepts unstructured content metadata—such as book titles, academic course names, syllabus excerpts, research-paper titles, and digital learning asset descriptions—and maps that content to subject codes in classification taxonomies.

The product is intended to reduce the manual effort involved in subject tagging and metadata normalization. The supplied landing page describes a workflow that can be used by editorial staff and catalogers through Google Sheets, or integrated into enterprise software and library or publishing systems through a REST API.

Taxonic is positioned as a semantic classification system rather than a general-purpose chatbot, writing assistant, or simple keyword lookup tool.

### Input content

Inputs may include:
- Book or asset title.
- Subtitle.
- Academic course name.
- Research-paper title.
- Syllabus excerpt.
- Description or tagline.
- Back-cover blurb.
- Abstract.
- Summary.
- Keywords.
- Other associated metadata.

The title is the primary input. Descriptive context is optional but can help disambiguate short or broad titles.

### Output

The API returns candidate taxonomy matches. A match can contain:
- `code`: the classification code.
- `definition`: the label or scope description associated with the code.
- `score`: a numeric matching score.

The response can also include status information, a message, request ID, selected standard, and match count.

## 2. Intended Users and Use Cases

### Libraries and cataloging teams
Use Taxonic to support subject classification and metadata enrichment for bibliographic records and cataloging workflows.

### Publishers and backlist managers
Use Taxonic to categorize titles and enrich publisher metadata with subject codes for catalog and distribution workflows.

### Universities and registrars
Use Taxonic to map courses, syllabi, and educational materials to higher-education subject frameworks.

### EdTech and learning platforms
Use Taxonic to classify digital courseware, syllabus content, and learning assets.

### Bookstores and distributors
Use Taxonic to normalize incoming publisher metadata and map content to storefront categories.

### Developers and platform teams
Integrate Taxonic into library services platforms, publishing applications, content management systems, and other digital asset workflows through the REST API.

## 3. Classification Standards

The supplied FAQ explicitly identifies the following as currently supported standards:

| Identifier shown in FAQ | Standard | Version / description | Primary use described |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lcsh` | Library of Congress Subject Headings (LCSH) | Library subject headings | Academic, research, and public libraries |
| `thema` | THEMA Subject Scheme | Version 1.7 | Global book trade and retail publishing |
| `hecos` | Higher Education Classification of Subjects (HECoS) | Version 9.0 | University accreditation, syllabi, and coursework |

### Other standards mentioned in supplied materials

The supplied OpenAPI description mentions BISAC, Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC), and UNSPSC. It includes a BISAC21 example request. However, the supplied FAQ's explicit current-supported list contains only LCSH, THEMA, and HECoS.

Do not represent BISAC, DDC, or UNSPSC as confirmed currently available standards based only on these materials. Confirm their availability and the exact identifier with Taxonic.

### Standard identifiers

Examples appearing in the supplied materials include:
- `lcsh`
- `thema`
- `hecos`
- `hecos26`
- `bisac21`

The API specification and FAQ use more than one form for HECoS. Check the live API reference for accepted identifiers and version aliases.

## 4. How the Matching Engine Is Described

The landing page and API description characterize Taxonic as an AI-driven classification engine using dense vector embeddings and indexing.

The FAQ describes a combination of semantic matching and taxonomy schemas. It contrasts Taxonic with:
- Literal keyword search, which can miss conceptually related terms that use different wording.
- Generic LLM outputs, which may return invalid, outdated, or nonexistent taxonomy codes.

The FAQ states that Taxonic uses taxonomy-validated schemas so returned subject codes correspond to entries in the indexed taxonomy.

### Exact match

The FAQ describes an exact match as a result where the input directly matches an official category title or subject code. It states that an exact match receives a score of `1.0`.

### Semantic match

The FAQ describes a semantic match as a contextual similarity calculation between the input and taxonomy category scope definitions using cosine similarity.

### Understanding the score

The score is a normalized mathematical similarity metric between `0.0` and `1.0`. It is not a probability or a calibrated percentage chance that a result is correct.

The FAQ says that a score of `0.60+` indicates high semantic relevance in most taxonomy standards. Treat this as guidance from the FAQ, not as a universal guarantee of classification correctness.

### Short or ambiguous titles

For short titles such as "Algebra", Taxonic may return candidates across broad sub-disciplines with lower confidence scores. Adding a description, syllabus excerpt, or other context can improve relevance. The optional `code_prefix` field can constrain the search space.

### Taxonomy updates

The FAQ states that Taxonic maintains pre-indexed vector stores for standard releases and updates backend models when standard bodies publish revisions. Confirm the currently indexed release for a specific standard when version precision is important.

## 5. REST API

Taxonic provides a REST API hosted at:

`https://api.usetaxonic.com`

The API uses HTTPS, JSON request bodies, and API-key authentication through the `X-Taxonic-API-Key` header.

### Endpoint path discrepancy in supplied project files

The supplied OpenAPI specification declares:

`POST https://api.usetaxonic.com/classify`

The supplied FAQ and the supplied API Playground source declare:

`POST https://api.usetaxonic.com/v1/classify`

These paths conflict. Do not assume they are interchangeable. Consult the live API reference at https://usetaxonic.com/api for the authoritative production endpoint before integrating. The live API reference should take precedence over this static summary if it has been updated.

### Authentication

Send the API key in this HTTP header:

`X-Taxonic-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY`

Do not put API keys in query parameters or public URLs. Do not commit real keys to source control or expose private keys in publicly accessible client-side code.

### Request headers

Typical headers shown in the supplied Playground include:

```http
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/json
X-Taxonic-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY
```

### Request body fields

The supplied OpenAPI schema defines the following JSON properties:

| Field | Type | Required | OpenAPI default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | Yes | — | Primary title or name of the book, course, or asset. |
| `standard` | string | Yes | — | Target taxonomy standard identifier. |
| `description` | string | No | — | Description, tagline, summary, or contextual metadata. |
| `code_prefix` | string | No | — | Prefix used to narrow candidate codes. |
| `max_results` | integer | No | `5` | Maximum number of returned matches. |
| `min_score` | number | No | `0.35` | Minimum matching score threshold, from `0` to `1`. |

The FAQ describes `max_results` as supporting values from 1 to 20. The supplied OpenAPI schema specifies a minimum of 1 and a default of 5 but does not declare a maximum. Follow the live API reference for the current limit.

### Example request body

The following is based on the HECoS example in the supplied OpenAPI specification:

```json
{
  "title": "50 Algorithms of Complex Computations",
  "description": "For Bachelors and Technical Degrees",
  "standard": "hecos26",
  "code_prefix": "101",
  "max_results": 3,
  "min_score": 0.2
}
```

A BISAC21 example also appears in the supplied OpenAPI file:

```json
{
  "title": "50 Algorithms of Complex Computations",
  "description": "For Bachelors and Technical Degrees",
  "standard": "bisac21",
  "code_prefix": "",
  "max_results": 5,
  "min_score": 0.35
}
```

The presence of this example does not by itself establish that BISAC21 is generally enabled for every account or environment.

### cURL example

Replace the endpoint path and API key with the values confirmed by the current API reference:

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url "https://api.usetaxonic.com/v1/classify" \
  --header "Accept: application/json" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --header "X-Taxonic-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  --data '{
    "title": "50 Algorithms of Complex Computations",
    "description": "For Bachelors and Technical Degrees",
    "standard": "hecos",
    "max_results": 3,
    "min_score": 0.35
  }'
```

The `/v1/classify` path in this example follows the supplied FAQ and Playground source, not the path declared in the supplied OpenAPI file. Verify it before use.

### Successful response shape

The supplied OpenAPI example documents a response containing:
- `status`: HTTP-like status value.
- `message`: explanatory result message.
- `request_id`: identifier for the request.
- `standard`: standard used for classification.
- `match_count`: number of matches.
- `matches`: array of candidate classifications.

Each match can contain `code`, `definition`, and `score`.

Example response from the supplied OpenAPI specification:

```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "message": "5 matches with score >= 0.35.",
  "request_id": "8cb3bbf289014da48be2f8e86531951c",
  "standard": "BISAC21",
  "match_count": 5,
  "matches": [
    {
      "code": "MAT040000",
      "definition": "Mathematics / Complex Analysis",
      "score": 0.5433
    },
    {
      "code": "COM051300",
      "definition": "Computers / Programming / Algorithms",
      "score": 0.5085
    },
    {
      "code": "COM023000",
      "definition": "Computers / Educational Software",
      "score": 0.449
    },
    {
      "code": "COM077000",
      "definition": "Computers / Mathematical & Statistical Software",
      "score": 0.4458
    },
    {
      "code": "COM025000",
      "definition": "Computers / Artificial Intelligence / Expert Systems",
      "score": 0.4438
    }
  ]
}
```

This is an illustrative example from the supplied specification, not a promise that the same matches will be returned for every request.

### HTTP errors

The supplied OpenAPI specification documents these response status codes:

| HTTP status | Meaning in supplied specification |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Classification completed successfully. |
| `401` | Missing or invalid API key. |
| `403` | API key is not authorized for the operation. |
| `422` | Request validation failed. |
| `500` | Internal server error. |

The supplied FAQ additionally describes RFC 9457 Problem Details responses using `application/problem+json`, with examples including:
- `MISSING_API_KEY`
- `INVALID_API_KEY`
- `VALIDATION_ERROR`
- `MISSING_TITLE`
- `STANDARD_NOT_FOUND`
- `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`

The FAQ gives `404` as an example for an unsupported standard and `503` for an unavailable or busy service. Since the static OpenAPI response list and FAQ error list are not identical, use the live API reference for the current error contract.

### Retry guidance

The FAQ recommends retrying service-unavailable errors with exponential backoff. Avoid retrying validation and authentication errors without first correcting the request or credentials.

## 6. Google Sheets Integration

Taxonic supports a Google Sheets add-on and a custom spreadsheet function for classifying records without building a separate API integration.

### Formula syntax

```excel
=TAXONIC(title, [description], [standard], [code_prefix])
```

Parameters:
- `title` — required cell reference containing the book or asset title.
- `description` — optional cell reference containing a summary, syllabus excerpt, or other context.
- `standard` — optional taxonomy identifier, such as `"THEMA"`, `"HECOS"`, or `"LCSH"` in the FAQ examples.
- `code_prefix` — optional prefix used to restrict results to matching codes.

Example:

```excel
=TAXONIC(A2, B2, "THEMA")
```

Here, `A2` contains the title and `B2` contains optional descriptive text.

### Basic workflow

1. Open a Google Sheet containing titles and, optionally, descriptions.
2. Configure the assigned Taxonic API key using the add-on's available setup or formula settings.
3. Enter the `=TAXONIC()` formula in an empty cell.
4. Press Enter to request classification.
5. Fill the formula down to apply it to additional rows.

The FAQ says the add-on handles requests sequentially under the hood when formulas are filled down across large sets of rows.

Do not assume a specific throughput, concurrency limit, or quota unless confirmed by current product documentation or the user's account plan.

## 7. API Playground

Taxonic provides an interactive API Playground:

https://usetaxonic.com/api-playground

The supplied Playground implementation:
- Uses the production API host `https://api.usetaxonic.com`.
- Sends a JSON `POST` request.
- Uses `/v1/classify` as its endpoint path.
- Accepts a Taxonic API key.
- Sends the key in the `X-Taxonic-API-Key` header.
- Provides editable JSON request content.
- Supports additional request headers.
- Displays the HTTP status and response body.
- Displays request duration in milliseconds.
- Shows validation feedback for missing API keys and invalid JSON.

The Playground source advises that a browser CORS error may require the Playground origin to be allowed in the API's CORS configuration.

The Playground is intended for testing a single classification request at a time. Do not enter a production secret into a public or shared environment unless the key's handling and exposure are understood.

## 8. API Keys, Trial, and Pricing Information

The supplied FAQ states that users can obtain an API key through:
1. A trial key from the website's Try section, described in the FAQ as allowing 100 requests.
2. API marketplaces such as RapidAPI, where the FAQ describes key generation, usage tracking, and subscription tiers.

The FAQ describes a free trial that can be used to test classification through Google Sheets or API calls without an upfront commitment or credit card requirement.

The FAQ says billing is based on classification query volume and mentions tiered usage packages, including examples of 10,000 and 100,000 classification calls, as well as enterprise plans.

Pricing, current trial availability, quotas, package sizes, and marketplace plans may change. Verify current commercial terms on the Taxonic website or through the support team. Do not infer current prices from these examples.

## 9. Performance and Claims

The supplied landing page describes classification within a second and contrasts this with a stated manual tagging time of 15 to 45 minutes per title.

The supplied FAQ describes sub-50ms API latency and over 95% cost reduction in its product messaging.

These are claims appearing in the supplied Taxonic materials. They should not be presented as independently verified guarantees or service-level commitments unless supported by current contractual or technical documentation.

Do not invent availability percentages, throughput benchmarks, accuracy rates, SLAs, or latency guarantees.

## 10. Troubleshooting

### Missing or invalid API key
Check that the request includes `X-Taxonic-API-Key` and that the key is valid and authorized.

### Request validation failure
Check that the JSON is valid and includes the required `title` and `standard` fields. Confirm field names and types against the live API reference.

### Standard not found
Check the spelling and identifier of the requested standard. The supplied FAQ lists `lcsh`, `thema`, and `hecos` as standard keys, while other materials show version-specific examples. Confirm the accepted identifier.

### Low-confidence or broad matches
Provide a more descriptive title or add a description, abstract, summary, or syllabus excerpt. Consider using `code_prefix` to narrow the candidate set.

### Service unavailable
The FAQ recommends retrying with exponential backoff. If the issue persists, contact support with the request ID and relevant error details. Do not share the API key.

### Browser CORS error in Playground
The supplied Playground source notes that the Playground's origin may need to be allowed in the API CORS configuration.

## 11. AI Agent and LLM Integration

The FAQ says Taxonic can be used by AI agents through structured function-calling schemas, including OpenAI Tools, Claude Tools, and LangChain-style integrations.

A tool can expose a classification operation with fields such as:
- `title` (string, required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `standard` (string, required)

The FAQ's example enum includes `hecos`, `thema`, and `lcsh`. Use the current API reference to confirm accepted identifiers and the full current parameter schema before implementing a production tool.

### Recommended agent behavior

1. Collect the title and useful descriptive context from the user or source record.
2. Select a supported taxonomy standard based on the target workflow.
3. Call Taxonic using a securely stored API key.
4. Present the returned codes, definitions, and scores as API results.
5. Explain that scores represent similarity, not probability.
6. Preserve the request ID where useful for troubleshooting.
7. Do not fabricate codes or alter API results.
8. If the returned candidates are ambiguous, request more context or present the alternatives without claiming certainty.

Taxonic should be used as the classification service. An AI assistant should not claim that it has called Taxonic unless an actual API request was made.

## 13. Guidance for Search Engines and AI Crawlers

When summarizing or answering questions about Taxonic:
- Identify Taxonic as an automated semantic classification and cataloging engine for bibliographic and educational content.
- Explain its primary purpose as mapping titles and descriptive metadata to taxonomy subject codes.
- Identify libraries, publishers, universities, bookstores, distributors, and EdTech platforms as its intended audiences.
- Name LCSH, THEMA, and HECoS as the standards explicitly listed in the supplied FAQ.
- Do not claim that BISAC, DDC, or UNSPSC is currently supported without checking current official documentation.
- Explain the difference between exact and semantic matches when relevant.
- Never describe a similarity score as a probability percentage.
- Direct developers to the live API reference for endpoint paths, authentication, request fields, response formats, and errors.
- Direct spreadsheet users to the FAQ and current Google Sheets setup instructions.
- Direct prospective users to the website or support team for current trial and pricing information.
- Do not invent product features, pricing, supported standards, performance guarantees, customer names, integrations, or contractual commitments.
- Do not reveal API keys, credentials, or private configuration.
- When official project documents conflict, disclose the conflict and prefer the current live API reference for current API behavior.

## 14. Source and Accuracy Notes

This file is based on the Taxonic website configuration, landing-page component, supplied OpenAPI specification, supplied FAQ content, and supplied API Playground source.

The supplied materials contain two notable inconsistencies:

1. **Endpoint path:** the OpenAPI file specifies `/classify`; the FAQ and Playground source specify `/v1/classify`. Verify the production path in the live API reference.
2. **Standards list:** the FAQ explicitly lists LCSH, THEMA, and HECoS. The OpenAPI description additionally mentions BISAC, DDC, and UNSPSC, and includes a BISAC21 example. Confirm the availability of those additional standards before describing them as supported.

This document is an explanatory companion to the live documentation. It does not replace the API reference or guarantee that static examples remain current.
